title:
VECTORS,
(VECTOR GEOMETRY PROOFS)
objective: LO: I can use vectors to prove geometric results involving midpoints, parallel lines, and collinear points.

content.text: In vector geometry, we express journeys around a shape in terms of vectors a and b. If two vectors are parallel (scalar multiples), the lines are parallel.
Key strategies: To prove collinearity, show one vector is a scalar multiple of another AND they share a common point. The midpoint of AB has position vector &frac{1}{2}(a + b).

examples.expr: Midpoint M of AB: OM = &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
If PQ = kRS, then PQ is parallel to RS

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Express unknown vectors as journeys using known vectors. Parallel means scalar multiple; collinear needs shared point too.
key_idea.caption: Travel from A to O (which is -a), then O to B (which is +b)

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – expressing a vector
modelled_examples.question: OA = a, OB = b. Express AB in terms of a and b.
modelled_examples.explanation: Go backwards along a, then forwards along b.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – finding a midpoint
modelled_examples.question: M is the midpoint of AB. OA = a, OB = b. Find OM.
modelled_examples.explanation: The midpoint is the average of the position vectors.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – proving lines are parallel
modelled_examples.question: OA = a, OB = b. M is midpoint of OA, N is midpoint of OB. Show MN is parallel to AB.
steps: AB = b - a, so MN = &frac{1}{2}AB. Parallel.
modelled_examples.explanation: MN is a scalar multiple of AB, proving they are parallel.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – proving collinearity
modelled_examples.question: OA = a, OB = 3a. Show O, A, B are collinear.
steps: OA = a and AB = 2a: AB = 2(OA), same direction, shared point A
modelled_examples.explanation: AB is a scalar multiple of OA and they share point A.
